verses.zh: （大卫的诗。）不要为作恶的心怀不平，也不要向那行不义的生出嫉妒。
verses.en: By David.Do not fret[NOTE:1] when wicked men seem to succeed.[NOTE:2] Do not envy evildoers.
notes: Psalm 37. The psalmist urges his audience not to envy the wicked, but to trust in and obey the Lord, for he will destroy sinners and preserve the godly. When the smoke of judgment clears, the wicked will be gone, but the godly will remain and inherit God’s promised blessings. The psalm is an acrostic; every other verse begins with a successive letter of the Hebrew alphabet.

The verb form is singular (see vv. 3-10 as well, where the second person verbs and pronouns are also singular). The psalmist’s exhortation has a wisdom flavor to it; it is personalized for each member of his audience.

verses.zh: 因为他们如草快被割下，又如青菜快要枯干。
verses.en: For they will quickly dry up like grass,and wither away like plants.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “over sinners.” The context indicates that the psalmist has in mind the apparent power and success of sinners. See v. 7b.

verses.zh: 你当倚靠耶和华而行善，住在地上，以他的信实为粮；
verses.en: Trust in the Lord and do what is right.Settle in the land and maintain your integrity.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “like green vegetation.”

verses.zh: 又要以耶和华为乐，他就将你心里所求的赐给你。
verses.en: Then you will take delight in the Lord,[NOTE:1] and he will answer your prayers.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “tend integrity.” The verb רָעָה (raʿah, “tend, shepherd”) is probably used here in the sense of “watch over, guard.” The noun אֱמוּנָה (ʾemunah, “faithfulness, honesty, integrity”) is understood as the direct object of the verb, though it could be taken as an adverbial accusative, “[feed] securely,” if the audience is likened to a flock of sheep.
Following the imperatives of v. 3 the prefixed verbal forms with vav (ו) in v. 4 indicate result. Faith and obedience (v. 3) will bring divine blessing (v. 4).

verses.zh: 当将你的事交托耶和华，并倚靠他，他就必成全。
verses.en: Commit your future to the Lord.[NOTE:1] Trust in him, and he will act on your behalf.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “and he will give you what you desire most.” Heb “and he will grant to you the requests of your heart.”
Heb “roll your way upon the Lord.” The noun “way” may refer here to one’s activities or course of life.

verses.zh: 他要使你的公义如光发出，使你的公平明如正午。
verses.en: He will vindicate you in broad daylight,and publicly defend your just cause.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “he will act.” Verse 6 explains what is meant; the Lord will vindicate those who trust in him.

verses.zh: 你当默然倚靠耶和华，耐性等候他；不要因那道路通达的和那恶谋成就的心怀不平。
verses.en: Wait patiently for the Lord![NOTE:1] Wait confidently[NOTE:2] for him!Do not fret over the apparent success of a sinner,[NOTE:3] a man who carries out wicked schemes.
notes: Heb “and he will bring out like light your vindication, and your just cause like noonday.”
Heb “Be quiet before the Lord!”

The Hebrew text has וְהִתְחוֹלֵל (vehitkholel, Hitpolel of חִיל, khil, “writhe with fear, suffer”) but this idea fits awkwardly here. The text should be changed to וְתוֹחֵל (vetokhel; Hiphil of יָחַל, yakhal, “wait”). It appears that the Hebrew text is the product of dittography: (1) the initial וה (vav-he) is accidentally repeated from the preceding word (יְהוָה, yehvah) and (2) the final ל (lamed) is accidentally repeated (note the preceding lamed and the initial lamed on the following form, לו).

verses.zh: 当止住怒气，离弃忿怒；不要心怀不平，以致作恶。
verses.en: Do not be angry and frustrated.[NOTE:1] Do not fret. That only leads to trouble.
notes: Heb “over one who causes his way to be successful.”

verses.zh: 因为作恶的必被剪除；惟有等候耶和华的必承受地土。
verses.en: Wicked men[NOTE:1] will be wiped out,[NOTE:2] but those who rely on the Lord are the ones who will possess the land.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “Refrain from anger! Abandon rage!”
Heb “for evil men.” The conjunction כִּי (ki, “for”) relates to the exhortations in v. 8; there is no reason to be frustrated, for the evildoers will be punished in due time.
Or “cut off, removed.”

verses.zh: 还有片时，恶人要归于无有；你就是细察他的住处也要归于无有。
verses.en: Evil men will soon disappear;[NOTE:1] you will stare at the spot where they once were, but they will be gone.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and those who wait on the Lord, they will possess the land.”
Heb “and yet, a little, there will be no wicked [one].”

verses.zh: 但谦卑人必承受地土，以丰盛的平安为乐。
verses.en: But the oppressed will possess the landand enjoy great prosperity.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and you will carefully look upon his place, but he will not be [there].” The singular is used here in a representative sense; the typical evildoer is in view.

verses.zh: 恶人设谋害义人，又向他咬牙。
verses.en: Evil men plot against the godly[NOTE:1] and viciously attack them.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and they will take delight in (see v. 4) abundance of peace.”
Or “innocent.” The singular is used here in a representative sense; the typical evildoer and the typical godly individual are in view.

verses.zh: 主要笑他，因见他受罚的日子将要来到。
verses.en: The Lord laughs in disgust[NOTE:1] at them,for he knows that their day is coming.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and gnashes at him with his teeth” (see Ps 35:16). The language may picture the evil men as wild animals. The active participles in v. 12 are used for purposes of dramatic description.

Heb “laughs.” As the next line indicates, this refers to derisive laughter (see 2:4). The Hebrew imperfect verbal form describes the action from the perspective of an eye-witness who is watching the divine response as it unfolds before his eyes.

verses.zh: 恶人已经弓上弦，刀出鞘，要打倒困苦穷乏的人，要杀害行动正直的人。
verses.en: Evil men draw their swordsand prepare their bows,to bring down[NOTE:1] the oppressed and needy,and to slaughter those who are godly.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “for he sees that his day is coming.” As the following context makes clear (vv. 15, 17, 19-20), “his day” refers to the time when God will destroy evildoers.
Heb “to cause to fall.”

verses.zh: 他们的刀必刺入自己的心；他们的弓必被折断。
verses.en: Their swords will pierce[NOTE:1] their own hearts,and their bows will be broken.
notes: Heb “the upright in way,” i.e., those who lead godly lives.

verses.zh: 一个义人所有的虽少，强过许多恶人的富余。
verses.en: The little bit that a godly man owns is better thanthe wealth of many evil men,[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “enter into.”

verses.zh: 因为恶人的膀臂必被折断；但耶和华是扶持义人。
verses.en: for evil men will lose their power,[NOTE:1] but the Lord sustains[NOTE:2] the godly.
notes: Heb “Better [is] a little to the godly one than the wealth of many evil ones.” The following verses explain why this is true. Though a godly individual may seem to have only meager possessions, he always has what he needs and will eventually possess the land. The wicked may prosper for a brief time, but will eventually be destroyed by divine judgment and lose everything.
Heb “for the arms of the evil ones will be broken.”

verses.zh: 耶和华知道完全人的日子；他们的产业要存到永远。
verses.en: The Lord watches over the innocent day by day,[NOTE:1] and they possess a permanent inheritance.[NOTE:2]
notes: The active participle here indicates this is characteristically true.
Heb “the Lord knows the days of the innocent ones.” He “knows” their days in the sense that he is intimately aware of and involved in their daily struggles. He meets their needs and sustains them.

verses.zh: 他们在急难的时候不致羞愧，在饥荒的日子必得饱足。
verses.en: They will not be ashamed when hard times come;[NOTE:1] when famine comes they will have enough to eat.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and their inheritance is forever.”
Heb “in a time of trouble.”

verses.zh: 恶人却要灭亡。耶和华的仇敌要像羊羔的脂油（或译：像草地的华美）；他们要消灭，要如烟消灭。
verses.en: But[NOTE:1] evil men will die;the Lord’s enemies will be incinerated[NOTE:2]—they will go up in smoke.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “in days of famine they will be satisfied.”
Or “for,” but Hebrew כִּי (ki) in this case would have to extend all the way back to v. 17a. Another option is to understand the particle as asseverative, “surely” (see v. 22).

The meaning of the MT (כִּיקַר כָּרִים [kiqar karim], “like what is precious among the pastures/rams”) is uncertain. One possibility is to take the noun כָּרִים as “pastures” and interpret “what is precious” as referring to flowers that blossom but then quickly disappear (see v. 2 and BDB 430 s.v. יָקָר 3). If כָּרִים is taken as “rams,” then “what is precious” might refer to the choicest portions of rams. The present translation follows a reading in the Dead Sea Scrolls (4QpPs37), כיקוד כורם (“like the burning of an oven”). The next line, which pictures the Lord’s enemies being consumed in smoke, supports this reading, which assumes confusion of the Hebrew letters ר (resh) and ד (dalet) at the end of the first word in the sequence.

verses.zh: 恶人借贷而不偿还；义人却恩待人，并且施舍。
verses.en: Evil men borrow, but do not repay their debt,but the godly show compassion and are generous.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “they perish in smoke, they perish.” In addition to repeating the verb for emphasis, the psalmist uses the perfect form of the verb to picture the enemies’ demise as if it had already taken place. In this way he draws attention to the certitude of their judgment.

verses.zh: 蒙耶和华赐福的必承受地土；被他咒诅的必被剪除。
verses.en: Surely[NOTE:1] those favored by the Lord[NOTE:2] will possess the land,but those rejected[NOTE:3] by him will be wiped out.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “an evil [man] borrows and does not repay, but a godly [man] is gracious and gives.” The singular forms are used in a representative sense; the typical evildoer and godly individual are in view. The three active participles and one imperfect (“repay”) draw attention to the characteristic behavior of the two types.
The particle כִּי (ki) is best understood as asseverative or emphatic here.
Heb “those blessed by him.” The pronoun “him” must refer to the Lord (see vv. 20, 23), so the referent has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “cursed.”

verses.zh: 义人的脚步被耶和华立定；他的道路，耶和华也喜爱。
verses.en: The Lord grants success to the onewhose behavior he finds commendable.[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “cut off”; or “removed” (see v. 9).

verses.zh: 他虽失脚也不致全身仆倒，因为耶和华用手搀扶他（或译：搀扶他的手）。
verses.en: Even if[NOTE:1] he trips, he will not fall headlong,[NOTE:2] for the Lord holds[NOTE:3] his hand.
notes: Heb “from the Lord the steps of a man are established, and in his way he delights.” The second line qualifies the first. The man whose behavior is commendable in God’s sight is the one whose ways are established by God. Another option is that the second line refers to the godly man delighting in God’s “way,” namely the lifestyle which he prescribes for men. In this case one might translate, “The Lord grants success to the one who desires to obey his commands.”
Other translation options for כִּי (ki) in this context are “when” (so NASB) or “though” (so NEB, NIV, NRSV).
Heb “be hurled down.”

verses.zh: 我从前年幼，现在年老，却未见过义人被弃，也未见过他的后裔讨饭。
verses.en: I was once young, now I am old.I have never seen the godly abandoned,or their children[NOTE:1] forced to search for food.[NOTE:2]
notes: The active participle indicates this is characteristically true. See v. 17.
Or “offspring”; Heb “seed.”

verses.zh: 他终日恩待人，借给人；他的后裔也蒙福！
verses.en: All day long they show compassion and lend to others,[NOTE:1] and their children[NOTE:2] are blessed.
notes: Heb “or his offspring searching for food.” The expression “search for food” also appears in Lam 1:11, where Jerusalem’s refugees are forced to search for food and to trade their valuable possessions for something to eat.
The active participles describe characteristic behavior.

verses.zh: 你当离恶行善，就可永远安居。
verses.en: Turn away from evil. Do what is right.[NOTE:1] Then you will enjoy lasting security.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “offspring”; Heb “seed.”
Or “Do good!” The imperatives are singular (see v. 1).

verses.zh: 因为，耶和华喜爱公平，不撇弃他的圣民；他们永蒙保佑，但恶人的后裔必被剪除。
verses.en: For the Lord promotes[NOTE:1] justice,and never abandons[NOTE:2] his faithful followers.They are permanently secure,[NOTE:3] but the children[NOTE:4] of the wicked are wiped out.[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “and dwell permanently.” The imperative with vav (ו) is best taken here as a result clause after the preceding imperatives.

Heb “loves.” The verb “loves” is here metonymic; the Lord’s commitment to principles of justice causes him to actively promote these principles as he governs the world. The active participle describes characteristic behavior.
The imperfect verbal form draws attention to this generalizing statement.
Or “protected forever.”
Or “offspring”; Heb “seed.”

verses.zh: 义人必承受地土，永居其上。
verses.en: The godly will possess the landand will dwell in it permanently.

verses.zh: 义人的口谈论智慧；他的舌头讲说公平。
verses.en: The godly speak wise wordsand promote justice.[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “cut off”; or “removed.” The perfect verbal forms in v. 28b state general truths.

verses.zh: 神的律法在他心里；他的脚总不滑跌。
verses.en: The law of their God controls their thinking;[NOTE:1] their[NOTE:2] feet do not slip.
notes: Heb “The mouth of the godly [one] utters wisdom, and his tongue speaks justice.” The singular form is used in a representative sense; the typical godly individual is in view. The imperfect verbal forms draw attention to the characteristic behavior of the godly.
Heb “the law of his God [is] in his heart.” The “heart” is here the seat of one’s thoughts and motives.

verses.zh: 恶人窥探义人，想要杀他。
verses.en: The wicked set an ambush for the godlyand try to kill them.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “his.” The pronoun has been translated as plural to agree with the representative or typical “godly” in v. 30.

verses.zh: 耶和华必不撇他在恶人手中；当审判的时候，也不定他的罪。
verses.en: But the Lord does not surrender the godly,or allow them to be condemned in a court of law.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “an evil [one] watches the godly [one] and seeks to kill him.” The singular forms are used in a representative sense; the typical evildoer and godly individual are in view. The active participles describe characteristic behavior.

verses.zh: 你当等候耶和华，遵守他的道，他就抬举你，使你承受地土；恶人被剪除的时候，你必看见。
verses.en: Rely[NOTE:1] on the Lord. Obey his commands.[NOTE:2] Then he will permit you[NOTE:3] to possess the land;you will see the demise of the wicked.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “the Lord does not abandon him into his hand or condemn him when he is judged.” The imperfects draw attention to the Lord’s characteristic behavior in this regard.
Or “wait.”

Heb “keep his way.” The Lord’s “way” refers here to the “conduct required” by the Lord. In Ps 25 the Lord’s “ways” are associated with his covenantal demands (see vv. 4, 9-10). See also Ps 119:3 (cf. vv. 1, 4), as well as Deut 8:6; 10:12; 11:22; 19:9; 26:17; 28:9; 30:16.
Heb “and he will lift you up.” The prefixed verbal form with vav (ו) is best taken here as a result clause following the imperatives in the preceding lines.

verses.zh: 我见过恶人大有势力，好像一根青翠树在本土生发。
verses.en: I have seen ruthless, wicked people[NOTE:1] growing in influence, like a green tree grows in its native soil.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “when evil men are cut off you will see.”
The Hebrew uses the representative singular again here.

verses.zh: 有人从那里经过，不料，他没有了；我也寻找他，却寻不着。
verses.en: But then one passes by, and suddenly they have disappeared.[NOTE:1] I looked for them, but they could not be found.
notes: Heb “being exposed [?] like a native, luxuriant.” The Hebrew form מִתְעָרֶה (mitʿareh) appears to be a Hitpael participle from עָרָה (ʿarah, “be exposed”), but this makes no sense in this context. Perhaps the form is a dialectal variant of מִתְעָלָה (“giving oneself an air of importance”; see Jer 51:3), from עָלָה (ʿalah, “go up”; see P. C. Craigie, Psalms 1-50 [WBC], 296). The noun אֶזְרָח (ʾezrakh, “native, full citizen”) refers elsewhere to people, but here, where it is collocated with “luxuriant, green,” it probably refers to a tree growing in native soil.

verses.zh: 你要细察那完全人，观看那正直人，因为和平人有好结局。
verses.en: Take note of the one who has integrity. Observe the upright.For the one who promotes peace has a future.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and he passes by and, look, he is not [there].” The subject of the verb “passes by” is probably indefinite, referring to any passerby. Some prefer to change the form to first person, “and I passed by” (cf. NEB; note the first person verbal forms in preceding verse and in the following line).

verses.zh: 至于犯法的人，必一同灭绝；恶人终必剪除。
verses.en: Sinful rebels are totally destroyed;[NOTE:1] the wicked have no future.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “for [there is] an end for a man of peace.” Some interpret אַחֲרִית (ʾakharit, “end”) as referring to offspring (see the next verse and Ps 109:13; cf. NEB, NRSV).
Or “destroyed together.” In this case the psalmist pictures judgment sweeping them away as a group.

verses.zh: 但义人得救是由于耶和华；他在患难时作他们的营寨。
verses.en: But the Lord delivers the godly;[NOTE:1] he protects them in times of trouble.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the end of evil men is cut off.” As in v. 37, some interpret אַחֲרִית (ʾakharit, “end”) as referring to offspring (see Ps 109:13). The perfect verbal forms in v. 38 probably express general truths. Another option is that they are used emphatically to state with certitude that the demise of the wicked is as good as done.
Heb “and the deliverance of the godly [ones] [is] from the Lord.”

verses.zh: 耶和华帮助他们，解救他们；他解救他们脱离恶人，把他们救出来，因为他们投靠他。
verses.en: The Lord helps them and rescues them;he rescues them from the wicked and delivers them,[NOTE:1] for they seek his protection.
notes: Heb “[he is] their place of refuge in a time of trouble.”
